primitives.name: Edge Condition Breakeven Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: An edge requires beating the closing line after vig (breakeven cover ≈ 0.5238 at -110; here we use simple >0.5 vs the consensus close as a first-pass filter).
primitives.assumptions: Market closes at -110; breakeven probability is fixed.

layer2.mapping: Edge detection kernel applied to cover rate distribution relative to breakeven.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of teams exceeding breakeven threshold

primitives.name: Team Aggregation of PFR Advanced Stats
primitives.verbatim_quote: Design: team-level aggregation of PFR advanced stats (weighted by targets / max-attempts QB row), signal in season t → next-season (t+1) team cover rate vs spreadLineHome (sign convention verified: positive = home favored).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_t': 'Team-level aggregated signal at time t (dimensionless)', 'w_i': 'Weight for player i (unitless)', 'S_i^t': "Player i's signal at time t (dimensionless)", 'n': 'Number of players (integer)'}
primitives.assumptions: Weights derived from target/max-attempts ratio; signal is stationary across seasons.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When individual player signals are washed out by aggregation.

layer2.mapping: Player-level signals aggregate into team-level predictive variables via weighted sum.

The core operator 'survivor_signal_to_cover_rate' operates on the premise that signals surviving falsifiers should predict future outcomes. However, the paper shows that while average separation and volume persist, they do not translate into actionable market edges. This is because the market efficiently incorporates such information, rendering persistence irrelevant. The edge condition 'edge_condition_breakeven' defines when a signal becomes profitable, requiring a probability greater than 0.5238 (breakeven at -110). Yet even if signals meet this condition, team aggregation erases their predictive power. The 'team_aggregation_pfr_stats' primitive aggregates player-level data into team-level predictors, but this process dilutes signal strength. The failure mode lies in assuming that statistical persistence implies economic value without accounting for market efficiency. The epistemic path reveals that the absence of an edge is not due to poor methodology but to the fundamental structure of efficient markets.
